task_1.title: Restore NMake dependency define quote formatting
task_1.description: Conan 2.27.1 partially reverts the NMake define-quoting change introduced in 2.27.0. Dependency-provided string defines are emitted using the previous quote style again to avoid malformed NMake compiler flags, while numeric handling remains intact and toolchain/profile define quoting is unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from Conan 2.27.0 to 2.27.1 restores correct NMake formatting for dependency-provided string defines so textual macro values are passed in the quote form NMake expects, without changing the existing handling of numeric, hexadecimal, empty, or bare defines.

expectation.grounded: In Conan's NMake integrations, dependency-side define formatting used by NMake dependency generation must revert the 2.27.0 quote-escaping regression for non-empty, non-numeric, non-hexadecimal NAME=value defines by emitting quoted string values without backslash-escaping the embedded quotes. Toolchain-originated define formatting must remain on its existing escaped-quote path, and bare defines, empty values, decimal integers, and hexadecimal values must preserve their prior output semantics.
expectation.conceptual: For NMake consumers, dependency macros with textual values should once again be generated as normal quoted string defines instead of over-escaped values. Other define forms should remain stable, and this update does not change the separate behavior of toolchain or profile supplied defines.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter observable NMake output for bare macros, empty-value macros, decimal numeric values, or hexadecimal values. Do not extend this revert to toolchain/profile define generation; only dependency-side textual value formatting changes in this release.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing NMake define behavior unchanged except for the regression affecting dependency string values, and do not treat this update as a full fix for toolchain/profile quoting issues.

behavior: NMake define formatting now distinguishes dependency-generated defines from toolchain-generated defines when deciding how to quote textual values.
A dependency define with a non-empty textual value is emitted with plain embedded quotes around the value instead of backslash-escaped embedded quotes.
Toolchain/profile-originated defines continue to use the escaped-quote form for textual values.
Defines without a value, with an empty value, or with decimal or hexadecimal numeric values keep the existing non-string formatting behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When an NMake dependency define contains only a macro name, it should still be generated as a standard define without adding a value.
When an NMake dependency define contains an empty value, it should remain an empty-value define rather than being converted into a quoted string.
When an NMake dependency define contains a decimal or hexadecimal numeric value, it should be generated as a numeric define without string-style quoting.
When an NMake dependency define contains a non-numeric textual value, it should be generated with plain embedded quotes around the value rather than escaped embedded quotes.
When a define comes from the toolchain or profile path instead of dependency metadata, its existing escaped-quote behavior should remain unchanged in 2.27.1.
